subject: science
passage: Most blue whales migrate long distances each year, feeding in cold waters near the poles in summer and moving to warmer waters in winter. The blue whales seen off the southern coast of Sri Lanka, however, are spotted in every month of the year. Marine biologist Nuwan Jayasinghe hypothesizes that these whales do not migrate at all but stay in the waters around Sri Lanka all year.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly support Jayasinghe's hypothesis?

choices.A: Photographs of individual whales, identified by tail shape, show the same animals off Sri Lanka in both summer and winter.
choices.B: Tourist boats that take visitors to see the whales operate mostly between November and April, when the sea is calm.
choices.C: Whales photographed off Sri Lanka in summer have never been seen there again in any later season.
choices.D: Blue whales off Sri Lanka feed mainly on shrimplike animals that are plentiful in the area throughout the year.

explanation.why: The fact that whales are seen in every month could mean that the same whales stay or that different whales pass through. Jayasinghe claims the first. The best support is evidence that the very same individuals are present in different seasons, which photographs of recognizable tails can provide.
explanation.A: Correct. Seeing the same individual whales in different seasons shows that they stay rather than migrate.
explanation.B: Incorrect. When tourists go whale watching has nothing to do with where the whales spend the year.
explanation.C: Incorrect. If the summer whales are never seen again, different whales are passing through, which suggests migration rather than staying.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Plentiful food might make staying possible, but it does not show that the whales actually stay.
